sentences.text: Therizinosaurus was a massive creature that could reach lengths of 9 to 10 meters, stand 4 to 5 meters tall, and weigh over 5 tons.

It possessed robust forelimbs with three fingers bearing stiffened, elongated claws that curved only at the tips, holding the record for the longest known manual claws of any land animal, exceeding 50 cm in length.
This dinosaur likely had a wide torso and a long neck, functioning as a slow-moving browser with a beak used for processing food.
The first remains were discovered in 1948 by a Mongolian expedition in the Gobi Desert.
Evgeny Maleev formally described the genus in 1954, establishing Therizinosaurus cheloniformis as the type species.
Fossils are known from the Nemegt Formation.
Analysis of the arms showed they were resistant to stress, suggesting they were used for both foraging and self-defense.
Researchers have considered the body plan of Therizinosaurus and Chalicotherium an example of convergent evolution between a mammal and a dinosaur.
Therizinosaurus is classified within the dinosaur clade Theropoda, specifically as a maniraptoran, and most scientific analyses recover it within the family Therizinosauridae.
The genus was originally assigned to its own family, Therizinosauridae, because it differed significantly from other known taxa.
The genus contains only one known species, Therizinosaurus cheloniformis.
Therizinosaurus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically in the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago, approximately 70 million years ago.

Historical debates regarding the classification of Therizinosaurus ranged from sauropodomorphs and ornithischians to theropods, with Maleev initially proposing it belonged to a turtle-like reptile. In 1970, Anatoly K. Rozhdestvensky suggested it was a theropod rather than a turtle, though he later re-identified some fragments of the holotype as sauropod remains based on their shape.
